Event-derived temporal features such as cadence, stride time, swing time, stance time, temporal asymmetry, double-support overlap, and U-turn duration are traceable to the metadata/events. Approximate straight walking speed, step length, and stride length are derived from the protocol distance and event counts, so they must not be presented as true foot-trajectory measurements. | source: clinical_gait_signals_2025 (Clinical Gait Signals paper and bundled plot_data.py event definitions)

Data_2 progression: speed, cadence, step length, and stride length: Perry and Burnfield frame walking speed, cadence, step length, stride length, and stride timing as linked distance-time gait descriptors. For Data_2, reduced approximate speed together with reduced approximate step or stride length supports an interpretation of reduced forward progression. Cadence should be interpreted with step and stride length: low cadence suggests slower stepping frequency, while high cadence with short steps can indicate a short-step timing strategy. Pathology-aware interpretation without diagnosis: The local gait-analysis source set supports cautious pathology-aware interpretation without making a new diagnosis. In CVA/stroke-labeled cases, reduced speed, shorter steps, and left-right temporal asymmetry are consistent with asymmetric or hemiparetic gait interpretation. In Parkinson disease-labeled cases, short step or stride length with cadence changes can support a short-step Parkinsonian pattern when grounded in the case values. In hip or knee osteoarthritis-labeled cases, slower speed and increased double support can support cautious or load-avoidance interpretation. In neuropathy-labeled cases, variability, asymmetry, and increased support time should be framed as possible stability-control findings rather than proof of sensory loss. | source: pathological_gait_local_review_set (PATHOLOGICAL_GAIT_SOURCE_COVERAGE_2026-06-14.md plus local PDFs)

Data_2 biomechanical feature provenance and limits: The Clinical Gait Signals dataset provides wearable IMU trials with detected toe-off and heel-strike events, U-turn boundaries, sampling frequency, cohort labels, pathology labels, visual gait assessment, and pathology-specific clinical scores. Event-derived temporal features such as cadence, stride time, swing time, stance time, temporal asymmetry, double-support overlap, and U-turn duration are traceable to the metadata/events. Approximate straight walking speed, step length, and stride length are derived from the protocol distance and event counts, so they must not be presented as true foot-trajectory measurements. | source: clinical_gait_signals_2025 (Clinical Gait Signals paper and bundled plot_data.py event definitions)

In Parkinson disease-labeled cases, short step or stride length with cadence changes can support a short-step Parkinsonian pattern when grounded in the case values. In hip or knee osteoarthritis-labeled cases, slower speed and increased double support can support cautious or load-avoidance interpretation.
